items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Altogether we wound up with... Oh, Edward Griffin was the tenor saxophone; we called him Bubbus -- Bubbus Griffin... And that little band went on for I guess two or three years... I think Bubbus went with him.

ctx.x: not. But anyway, he came by my house one day and told me, told us rather, that he'd like to form this band if we could get some more guys. Of course, we told him, sure, we could.

There was a guy that lived in Oswald Gibson's neighborhood. As a matter of fact, they kind of grew up together, I guess. His name was George Brown. Later they gave him the name of Dude Brown, for certain reasons which maybe I'll get a chance to talk about later. But Dude Brown, George Brown was a drummer. A fellow, William Eldridge, who is a cousin to Roy Eldridge, was also at Armstrong High School, played bass. And we had a trumpet player, our first trumpet player, that later went to Philadelphia and later…

Now, Oswald Gibson, Frank Wess and Nathan Washington (because Nathan was his name) all played alto saxophones. Bubbus was the only one that played tenor. So, this fellow Billy Roberts said, "Look, we can't have three alto saxophones
